title: The dependencies DP-03, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10 and DP-19 add are absent from this story's build and contract lists, and no fake is named for the reference data or the decision record
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP table); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 17, 20 and 43; TSD P6 Communications v2 T2 and T5.3; WP B-P6-04 story line for RWB-P6-E1007-APP (H [] and C [RWB-P2-E1007-CON])
section: Metadata table (Depends on (build), Contract dependencies), section 3 Preconditions, 12.2 REST consumed, 12.4 Events consumed, 12.6 Schedules, 13 Solution plan
description: The DP table adds six H rows and one C row to this story: RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (DP-03), RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON (DP-07), RWB-PLT-TE006-CON (DP-09), RWB-PLT-E1071-CON (DP-10) and RWB-PLT-N001-CON (DP-19). The story's plan lists hold Depends on (build) None and Contract dependencies RWB-P2-E1007-CON only, so the reference-data contract of rwb-case, the reference-data library, the decision-record library, the outbox and inbox library, the workflow kit and the gateway-bff route are named in the pattern table and in the text but are dependencies of nothing. The story cannot run without them: the eligible state set and the three lists come from the reference-data contract, the decision record is written where a rule decides the eligible set, the event is written to the outbox, the run is a workflow on task queue rwb-comms, and the run state is read through the composite route. No source gives this story a fake of its own for the reference data or the decision record, so the story names the published reference values and the local library as its fakes and records the absence here rather than adding rows to the plan.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 rows DP-03 'H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON', DP-07 'H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON', DP-09 'H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON', DP-10 'H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON', DP-19 'H RWB-PLT-N001-CON'; Architecture v5 slide 17 rwb-comms TMP 'Document: generate letter - Decision: child: approval - Integration: deliverFile (WIN letters)' and slide 20 'Every service ... outbox relay, inbox, Temporal worker ... decision_record'; WP B-P6-04 story line for RWB-P6-E1007-APP with H [] and C ['RWB-P2-E1007-CON'].
area: Communications (P6) outbound file producer: platform libraries and the rwb-case reference-data contract
proposed: Keep the plan's lists as they stand, keep the story at Day 1 with the P2 contract as its only build dependency, and build against the fakes of the six contracts until they publish. When the platform and reference-data stories publish, add the six rows to the plan, re-run the dependency check and replace each fake with the real contract in the same iteration.

title: The addressee and contact value reach the INT-14 file through a contract that is not in the story's contract list, and no source names the operation or its elements
source: DP-05 of Template and Rules v1 R5.5; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 9, 13, 37 and 45; Ownership Map tables (party_ext and contact_point_ext owned by P1); TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1 (DF-ACE-076 to DF-ACE-078); legacy RWB-E1-007 sections 4, 7 (AC2) and 11
section: Section 1 Story, section 3 Preconditions, section 8 BR4, section 11 Data, 12.2 REST consumed, section 17 Guardrails
description: The legacy adapter read recovery.v_ace_contact by contact_key in process and wrote the addressee and the address into the file it sent. Under DP-05 and ADR-010 only rwb-source-data reads the thirty recovery.v_ace_* views, the addressee, the address and the contact value never enter rwb_comms, and the file needs them as a token inside the build. The contract that serves that token is not in this story's contract list, which holds RWB-P2-E1007-CON only, and no source names the operation, its query or its element names. The consequence is stated in the story: the token is requested by notice.party_id at build time, is used inside the record set only, and is never stored, logged or put on an event or on the manifest.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 9 'only rwb-source-data reads the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views' and slide 37 'Views read only by rwb-source-data'; legacy RWB-E1-007 AC2 'Then each addressee and address is read from v_ace_contact by contact_key'; TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1 DF-ACE-076 contact_key, DF-ACE-077 person_key and DF-ACE-078 contact_value; WP B-P6-04 C list of RWB-P6-E1007-APP (RWB-P2-E1007-CON only).
area: Communications (P6) outbound file producer: addressee token
owner_role: Solution architect, with the P1 and P6 owners
proposed: Fix one read in the rwb-source-data contract that returns the postal addressee only, by party_id, with a 2 s budget and a fake, add that contract to this story's contract list, and keep the value out of rwb_comms, out of the event and out of every log.

title: DP-17 removes the INT-19 reporting extract and the INT-20 decision-log copy, so part of legacy RWB-E1-007 has no target and no replacement in this service
source: DP-17 of Template and Rules v1 R5.5; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 2, 8, 37 and 44; legacy RWB-E1-007 sections 2, 5, 12 (JOB-13 and JOB-15) and 16
section: Section 2 Business rationale, section 8 BR7, 12.6 Schedules, 12.9 Call-type summary, section 17 Guardrails, section 18 Traceability, section 19 Out of scope
description: The legacy story carried four outbound interfaces and four Quartz jobs, of which INT-19 (the nightly reporting extract, JOB-15) and INT-20 (the nightly decision-log copy, JOB-13) were files for the data lake. DP-17 removes the lake; Architecture v5 slides 2, 8 and 37 state that no Recovery service connects to the lake and that INT-19 and INT-20 are removed; slide 44 gives JOB-15 to rwb-reporting as an Airflow trigger with no data lake and JOB-13 to rwb-decision as continuous Kafka ingest. No source restates the two lake files on a target path in rwb-comms, so the story records them as removed with no replacement and asserts their absence (no lake client, no lake target, no lake delivery row, no adapter or endpoint for either interface ID) instead of restating a behaviour that has no owner here. The reporting projection is fed by the service's business events into rwb-reporting and the ledger by the shared decision-record topic, and both belong to other services.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 2 'Recovery has no connection to the data lake; INT-19/INT-20 are removed' and slide 37 (INT-19 and INT-20 removed); slide 44 rows JOB-13 'rwb-decision | ingest is continuous (Kafka)' and JOB-15 'rwb-reporting | Airflow trigger (no data lake)'; legacy RWB-E1-007 section 12 jobs table 'JOB-13 Decision log copy ... file to the data lake (INT-20)' and 'JOB-15 Reporting extract ... file to the data lake (INT-19)'; section 5 X1 to X8 carry no lake path.
area: Communications (P6) outbound file producer: retired lake interfaces
proposed: Record INT-19, INT-20, JOB-13 and JOB-15 as removed with no target in this service, keep the removal inside the story's scope as an assertion, and leave the reporting projection to rwb-reporting from the business events and the decision ledger to the shared decision-record topic. No lake file, lake copy or lake delivery row is created anywhere in the target.

title: The INT-14 record layout, the file pattern and the claim-check store of the built file are named by no source, and the document contract is not in the story's contract list
source: TSD P2 Integration v3 T2 (OutboundFileAdapter) and T3.1 (interface_config.file_pattern DF-OPS-141, outbound_item.payload_ref DF-OPS-171); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11 (claim-check) and 16 (Document: fetch file by ID, SAS link); Ownership Map tables (interface_config owned by P2, document owned by P5); legacy RWB-E1-007 section 12
section: Section 3 Preconditions, section 4 Flow, section 11 Data, 12.2 REST consumed, 12.5 Workflows and activities, 12.8 Contract fakes
description: The record set of the INT-14 file is built here, and the bytes have to be stored before the hand-off because no message, workflow input or log carries file content (Architecture v5 slide 11). Three points are unsettled by the sources. First, the owner of the WIN record layout and of the file pattern: the interface row is rwb-integration's per the Ownership Map, while the record set is built in rwb-comms, so the layout has to be read through the contract and never copied into a value file. Second, the operation that accepts the built file and returns its reference: the P2 table keeps only payload_ref, an attachment reference, and no source names the store call. Third, the owner of that store: the document hub is P5's and its contract is not in this story's contract list. The story therefore builds the record set to the layout of the interface row, stores the file behind a claim-check reference and records the three points as open, with a stub in the contract fakes.
evidence: TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1 DF-OPS-141 'file_pattern' and DF-OPS-171 'payload_ref ATTACHMENT' of outbound_item; Architecture v5 slide 11 (claim-check for files, no content on a message) and slide 16 rwb-document 'REST POST /documents (returns upload link)'; Ownership Map interface_config (P2) and document (P5); legacy RWB-E1-007 section 12 published interface 'OutboundFileRequest ... payloadRef'.
area: Communications (P6) outbound file producer: layout and claim-check object store
owner_role: Solution architect, with the P2 and P5 owners
proposed: Fix the record layout and the file pattern with the WIN interface owner and hold them as the interface row of rwb-integration, read through the contract; store the built file in the document hub behind a claim-check reference; add the document contract to the story's contract list; and pass only the reference in the manifest, never the content.

source: legacy RWB-E1-007 sections 13 and 16; TSD P2 Integration v3 change note (D-RCV-35) and T2; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.6; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8 and 44
section: Section 16 Test cases, section 17 Guardrails, section 18 Traceability, section 19 Out of scope
description: The legacy story removed the inbound FileLoadAdapter, FileCheckRunner and RecordLoader, the inbound folder listing, the file checks DQ-057 and DQ-059, the missing-file run row, JOB-09 File loads, interface_run and interface_signoff, and left TC-E1-007-05 (file missing at the cut-off) and TC-E1-007-06 (same file delivered twice) as identifiers with no behaviour. Their later home is ACE ingestion under RWB-ACE-001, which is not a story of this WP and not in the wave-1 build, and no P6 story restates an inbound check. The two identifiers still have to appear in the test table because they are the legacy test set of the key, so the story carries them as NFR rows that assert the absence of the inbound adapter, the folder listing, the two checks and the run table, and that name the behaviour as ACE ingestion and the EV-27 AceDataLate alert.

FileLoadAdapter, FileCheckRunner, RecordLoader, the inbound folder listing, the file checks DQ-057 and DQ-059, the missing-file run row, JOB-09 File loads, interface_run and interface_signoff' and the section 16 note on TC-E1-007-05 and TC-E1-007-06; TSD P2 Integration v3 change note 'the Workbench loads no source data (U1) ... the inbound file adapter, interface_run and interface_signoff are removed'; Architecture v5 slide 8 (ACE ingests every source) and slide 44 (JOB-09 is not a job of the target).

proposed: Keep the two identifiers as NFR rows that assert the absence of the inbound adapter, the folder listing, the two checks and the run table, state that the behaviour is ACE ingestion and the EV-27 AceDataLate alert, and close the two rows when the ACE ingestion story publishes its own checks.

title: No source defines a run record, a run operation or the right on the interface monitor for rwb-comms
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 T-A.1 (API-P6-001 to API-P6-011) and T6.1 (RBAC matrix); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 17, 20 and 43; legacy RWB-E1-007 sections 9, 12 and 15; TSD P2 Integration v3 T-A.1 (the item operations of P2)
section: Section 9 State transitions, section 10 Authority, 12.1 REST provided, section 15 Screens and states
description: The legacy story recorded the outbound run on outbound_item plus outbox_delivery and served the monitor from two admin endpoints of the same module. In the target both tables are rwb-integration's and the monitor is SCR-44, whose route, field list and merge order belong to the platform edge. The TSD P6 appendix T-A carries no run operation, and neither the P6 nor the P2 appendix names the right that a reader of the run state holds. The story therefore answers the run state from its own dispatch fields, the workflow run and the status the owner reports, with no run table; it provides one read and one producer rerun on /api/recovery/comms/v1 as its own design; it enforces the right at the edge for the screen path; and it applies DP-08 nowhere, because the guard story is not named in the sources.
evidence: TSD P6 Communications v2 T-A.1 endpoint inventory (API-P6-001 to API-P6-011, no run operation) and T6.1 RBAC matrix (RW-PLATADM: Documents R, Litigation absent); Architecture v5 slide 20 gateway-bff 'Owner service, one hop, in parallel for composite screens (2 s timeout, breaker per service)'; legacy RWB-E1-007 section 9 'There is no interface_run row: the outbound run record is outbound_item plus outbox_delivery'; section 15 'SCR-09 Exception queue (E1)' as the only monitor of the key.
area: Communications (P6) outbound file producer: run state, run operations and the interface monitor
owner_role: Solution architect and the gateway-bff owner
proposed: Answer the run state from the dispatch fields of the notices, the workflow run and the status the P2 contract returns, with no run table; provide one read and one rerun on the service base; enforce the right at gateway-bff for the screen path; and confirm with the edge owner whether a local guard is required on the operation itself.

title: RWB-P6-E1011-APP: the parameters and reference-data contracts of rwb-case and the rwb-source-data contract the run reads are missing from the story's C list
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-06, DP-07 and DP-11 and R3 default rulings; Ownership Map part tables (parameter_catalog, parameter_value, reference_row, reference_version to P3; data_product and data_contract to P1); TSD P1 v3 API-P1-009 and API-P1-003; API Specification v4 /admin/parameters (x-module P3); Legacy RWB-E1-011 sections 3 and 12

title: The notice barcode break is REC-09 in RWB-E1-011 and REC-05 in RWB-E1-055, where RWB-E1-011 uses REC-05 for the business-key orphan check
source: Legacy RWB-E1-011 sections 2, 7 AC7 and 19 (REC-05 business-key resolution; notice barcodes as REC-09); legacy RWB-E1-055 section 4 step 11 and section 8 BR5 (the barcode break as REC-05); FSD P1 v3 A2.11.2 (REC-05 business key); TSD P1 v3 T3.1 reconciliation_result note (REC-05 orphan)
description: Two legacy stories use the same check code for different checks: in RWB-E1-011 REC-05 resolves every account_key, person_key, asset_key, payment_code and contact_key on a Workbench table to its ACE view and lists the orphans, while RWB-E1-011 section 19 also assigns REC-09 to notice barcodes; in RWB-E1-055 REC-05 is the daily comparison of the notices sent to WIN with the barcodes returned, and the FSD P1 and TSD P1 keep REC-05 for the business-key resolution only. A reconciliation_result row keyed by rec_code alone cannot carry both meanings, and this story must number the check it owns without silently redefining the other.
evidence: RWB-E1-011 section 7 AC7 "the REC-05 result for the product group of the case is BREAK with 1 orphan" and section 19 "notice barcodes (REC-09, RWB-E1-055)"; RWB-E1-055 section 4 step 11 "compares the notices sent to WIN with the barcodes returned (REC-05)" and section 8 BR5 "REC-05"; FSD P1 v3 A2.11.2 check table row REC-05 business key; TSD P1 v3 reconciliation_result note "A REC-05 orphan raises a break to the data steward"
proposed: Settle the check numbering with the data steward before the wave-1 exit: keep REC-05 for the business-key orphan check of RWB-E1-011 and its result rows, give the notice barcode break its own code in both stories, and correct either RWB-E1-055 or the register so one code has one meaning

title: RWB-P6-E1011-APP: the data lake is removed, so the reconciliation and data quality extracts and the report built on them have no target
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17 and R6 retired rows; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 37 (no data lake), slide 44 JOB-15 and slide 15 P9 contract; Legacy RWB-E1-011 sections 3, 4 steps 10 to 12, 12 and 15; FSD P1 v3 A2.12.2 and AC-EXC-P1-012-02
description: The legacy publish step wrote a reconciliation extract and a data quality extract to the data lake through the INT-19 outbound adapter, and the Power BI report refreshed from them. Arch v5 removes the data lake and DP-17 removes INT-19 and INT-20, and rwb-reporting builds its read model from the business events and the projections of the services. proposed: Drop the two extracts and the INT-19 path from this key, serve the quality facts from GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/quality-results and settle with rwb-reporting how its report of the date reads them; record the decision in the Change Register against RWB-E1-014 and INT-19

title: RWB-P6-E1011-APP: no event is published because DP-09 is not in the pattern set, and no operation of rwb-reporting or rwb-source-data accepts the quality facts
source: Work Package B-P6-04 story line 56 (patterns without DP09); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09, DP-17 and R4; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15 (P9 IN and OUT), slide 42 (events of rwb-comms) and slide 43 (FileDelivered); TSD P1 v3 T-A.1 API-P1-003

title: RWB-P6-E1011-APP: the quality tables, the check codes, the run cadence and the two quality read operations are not named in any source
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 (no reconciliation or quality section, T2 and T3.1 tables only); FSD P6 Communications v3 (no quality or reconciliation section, measure "Notices with proof of delivery" only); Ownership Map part tables (reconciliation_result to P1); Legacy RWB-E1-011 sections 4 and 12
description: The module specification of rwb-comms declares the notice, template, merge_field and signature_request tables and no reconciliation or quality object, and the functional specification carries only the measure "Notices with proof of delivery, 100 percent" with no check, run, break list or report. The legacy key puts the result table reconciliation_result and the run record in rwb-source-data, which owns the enterprise reconciliation, and names no notice-level check, no check code, no cadence and no read operation. This story therefore designs three tables, two check names, one Schedule, one workflow and two read paths with no source behind their names.
evidence: TSD P6 Communications v2 T2 and T3.1 (notice, template, merge_field, signature_request only) and T5.3 (NoticeGenerated, NoticeDispatched, NoticeDelivered only); FSD P6 Communications v3 line 182 metric "Notices with proof of delivery - 100 percent - Decision log and Workbench records - Monthly" with no check section; Ownership Map v1 table reconciliation_result owner P1; RWB-E1-011 section 12 (job step, published interface used, reading the results)
proposed: Accept the design as the rwb-comms quality model of this story (comms_quality_run, comms_quality_result, comms_quality_break; REC-09 with the checks ACK and POD; one Schedule after the pod read; GET /quality-runs/{businessDate} and GET /quality-results) and carry the names into the API Specification, the schema folder and the batch and scheduling design at the next version

title: DP-08 is claimed while the authorise contract and the guard library are in no dependency list
source: Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-08; WP B-P6-04 story line for RWB-P6-E1019-APP; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 notes (permission data cached from rwb-access) and slide 41 (P4 owns Recovery roles as data); TSD P6 Communications v2 T6.2

title: The split of the legacy role, queue and membership data between rwb-case and rwb-access is not stated, and the membership read has no published operation
source: Ownership Map v1 (queue, queue_member and lov_value to P3; role, permission and masking_rule to P4); TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T3.1 and T3.2; TSD P6 Communications v2 T6.1 and T6.2; WP B-P6-04 read-only list
description: The legacy key holds ROLE, TEAM, QUEUE and QUEUE_MEMBER in one module and one schema. The ownership map puts queue, queue_member, lov_value and the reference tables with P3 and the roles, permissions and masking with P4, but no source says how far the split goes on the reading side: whether the role code a queue names is a P3 reference value or a P4 role key, and whether a reader asks P3 for the role list or P4. The P3 contract publishes GET /queues, GET /admin/lists/{listCode} and the two reference-load operations only, so a queue membership, capacity or member read has no REST operation at all, although the P3 story keeps an in-process CapacityService and QueueMembershipQuery. evidence: ownership.json entries queue P3, queue_member P3, lov_value P3, role P4, permission P4, masking_rule P4; RWB-P3-E1019-APP section 12.1 lists four operations and no membership read; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (P3 OUT) and slide 41

title: No source decides whether a reader keeps a local cache of the role and queue data
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 notes (permission data cached from rwb-access); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-01 and DP-15; Ownership Map v1
description: DP-01 forbids reading another service's tables, and the architecture says permission data is cached from rwb-access, but no document says whether a consumer may keep a queue or role cache in its own schema, for how long it lives, or how it is invalidated when the owner publishes a new version. A cached queue row in rwb_comms would be a copy of P3 reference data and would serve a superseded version after a rollback, which is exactly what REQ-CWC-006 promises never to happen. The story decides against a cache table; that decision is the story's own and no source supports or forbids it.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 14 notes; ownership.json holds no cache table for any service; RWB-P3-E1019-APP section 12.7 lists no cache and no consumer cache contract
proposed: State the caching rule for reference readers in the service template: a reader may cache for the life of one call only, and a longer-lived cache is a contract of the owner with a version and an invalidation event

title: The proof-record path, its fields and its right are this story's design, because no source names a proof-record operation
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2.md (appendix T-A); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (api); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E5-002 Endpoints)
description: The TSD P6 appendix T-A names eleven operations, of which only API-P6-001 (create a notice) and API-P6-002 (read a notice) touch a notice and neither records a proof; the story master names POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve, which the ownership map gives to S4. The path /notices/{noticeId}/proof-of-delivery, its request fields (delivery status, delivered or callback date, barcode where supplied), its Idempotency-Key rule and the Litigation C right on it are therefore the design of this story and not a value copied from a source. The path stays inside the service base of DP-13, but until the operation is published in the service API the edge, the tests and the S4 side have no shared shape for it.
evidence: TSD P6 T-A.1 API-P6-001 to API-P6-011 (no proof-record operation) and T-A.2 API-P6-002 (notice read, Litigation right R); ownership.json api 'POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve' owner S4, 'GET /notices/{noticeId}' owner P6; story master RWB-E5-002 Endpoints table; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-13.
proposed: Publish the write path, its request and answer fields and its right in the service API specification and the service contract story once the S4 contract is settled, so that the edge, the tests and the S4 side share one shape; until then this story's section 12.1 is the reference and the fields are marked as its design.

title: DP-03 and its decision-record library are missing from the pattern set and the build list of the e-signature key
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 T2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42 event 08 DecisionRecorded, producer all 19 services; plan split slices for RWB-P6-E2018-APP
description: RWB-E2-018 has no decision-log statement of its own, but the TSD P6 T2 pattern for the module requires the decision log entry before any change, and the target carries that record as event 08 DecisionRecorded on rwb.decision-record.v1 with every service as producer. The plan pattern set for the key is DP01, DP05, DP07, DP09, DP10, DP11, DP13, DP15 and DP19, so DP-03 is absent and the H list carries no RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, while the story still writes one decision record per request and per result. The dependency and the pattern row therefore have no plan home.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T2 says the CommunicationsService writes the decision log entry before any change; Architecture v5 slide 42 lists event 08 DecisionRecorded with producer all 19 and topic rwb.decision-record.v1; the slice RWB-P6-E2018-APP carries patterns DP01, DP05, DP07, DP09, DP10, DP11, DP13, DP15, DP19 and an H list without RWB-PLT-E1027-CON.
proposed: Add DP-03 and H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON to the slice RWB-P6-E2018-APP in the plan, or confirm that the local decision-record library is delivered by the platform release train; the story keeps writing one record per request and per applied result and cites this row until the plan is corrected.
